title: Reagents that sharpen bioelectric compartment borders reinforce normal patterning

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Reagents that sharpen bioelectric compartment borders reinforce normal patterning

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The BETSE model predicts that reagents that sharpen the borders between bioelectric compartments, such as the context-sensitive HCN2 channel, will reinforce normal developmental patterning, a prediction confirmed for HCN2 in vivo.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pai VP 2018, HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Most importantly, it predicts that reagents that sharpen borders between bioelectric compartments will reinforce normal patterning, thus identifying a context-sensitive HCN2 ion channel as an intervention tool.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pai VP, Pietak A, Willocq V, Ye B, Shi NQ, Levin M, “HCN2 Rescues brain defects by enforcing endogenous voltage pre-patterns”, Nature communications (2018), doi:10.1038/s41467-018-03334-5; section “Discussion”. Scope: Embryonic brain patterning in Xenopus; proposed more generally for bioelectrically patterned tissues

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2018-hcn2-18: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.54

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The HCN2 case and model can test the proposed relationship in one setting. The broader reagent-class mechanism is only partially covered and may conflate border sharpening with other channel effects.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define border sharpness as the spatial Vmem gradient between compartments, quantify how candidate reagents change that gradient, and test whether increased sharpness predicts improved morphology across interventions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
HCN2 is only one reagent and cannot establish the class-wide rule.

Border sharpness and normal patterning require explicit metrics.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Inside BETSE, swapping channel kinetics is an analysis that can support or weaken the idea that border-sharpening reagents, as a class, stabilize the pattern. The in vivo half of the claim is the HCN2 rescue, which does not sample the class. Channelpedia supplies the alternative kinetics, and the anatomical scores that would connect slope to patterning are not an open dataset. The model class is partly testable now; the tissue generalization is not.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define border sharpness as the spatial slope of Vmem between neural tube and lateral ectoderm, then relate that slope to a brain-patterning score for HCN2 and for other reagents that steepen the same border. The general prediction holds if steeper borders improve patterning across reagents; an HCN2-only benefit, or a steep border with worse patterning, would limit or refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A channel can improve patterning by a path other than a steeper voltage border.

Border sharpness itself was not deposited as a measured profile.

In vivo confirmation is a single reagent, HCN2.
